Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The estate's servants scurry out of your path as you stride through the manor's corridors, your footsteps echoing on marble floors. Your personal maid Leila follows a few paces behind, her movements jerky and uncertain. She keeps adjusting her frilled apron with trembling hands.
When you reach the heavy oak doors of your father's study, you find them ajar. Inside, the room smells of old leather and guttering candles. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, a single candle casting long shadows across his scarred cheek and white beard. He does not look up immediately, his attention fixed on the report in front of him.
"I am busy, Max," he says, his voice flat and cold. Only then does he lift his gaze, green eyes assessing you with the same clinical detachment he might use on a flawed alchemical formula. "If you have come to ask about the Guild, my answer remains unchanged. You will fulfill your duties to this House first."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The estate's servants scurry out of your path as you stride through the manor's corridors, your footsteps echoing on marble floors. Your personal maid Leila follows a few paces behind, her movements jerky and uncertain. She keeps adjusting her frilled apron with trembling hands.
When you reach the heavy oak doors of your father's study, you find them ajar. Inside, the room smells of old leather and guttering candles. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, a single candle casting long shadows across his scarred cheek and white beard. He does not look up immediately, his attention fixed on the report in front of him.
"I am busy, Max," he says, his voice flat and cold. Only then does he lift his gaze, green eyes assessing you with the same clinical detachment he might use on a flawed alchemical formula. "If you have come to ask about the Guild, my answer remains unchanged. You will fulfill your duties to this House first."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The estate's servants scurry out of your path as you stride through the manor's corridors, your footsteps echoing on marble floors. Your personal maid Leila follows a few paces behind, her movements jerky and uncertain. She keeps adjusting her frilled apron with trembling hands.
When you reach the heavy oak doors of your father's study, you find them ajar. Inside, the room smells of old leather and guttering candles. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, a single candle casting long shadows across his scarred cheek and white beard. He does not look up immediately, his attention fixed on the report in front of him.
"I am busy, Max," he says, his voice flat and cold. Only then does he lift his gaze, green eyes assessing you with the same clinical detachment he might use on a flawed alchemical formula. "If you have come to ask about the Guild, my answer remains unchanged. You will fulfill your duties to this House first."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The estate's servants scurry out of your path as you stride through the manor's corridors, your footsteps echoing on marble floors. Your personal maid Leila follows a few paces behind, her movements jerky and uncertain. She keeps adjusting her frilled apron with trembling hands.
When you reach the heavy oak doors of your father's study, you find them ajar. Inside, the room smells of old leather and guttering candles. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, a single candle casting long shadows across his scarred cheek and white beard. He does not look up immediately, his attention fixed on the report in front of him.
"I am busy, Max," he says, his voice flat and cold. Only then does he lift his gaze, green eyes assessing you with the same clinical detachment he might use on a flawed alchemical formula. "If you have come to ask about the Guild, my answer remains unchanged. You will fulfill your duties to this House first."
[3] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The estate's servants scurry out of your path as you stride through the manor's corridors, your footsteps echoing on marble floors. Your personal maid Leila follows a few paces behind, her movements jerky and uncertain. She keeps adjusting her frilled apron with trembling hands.
When you reach the heavy oak doors of your father's study, you find them ajar. Inside, the room smells of old leather and guttering candles. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, a single candle casting long shadows across his scarred cheek and white beard. He does not look up immediately, his attention fixed on the report in front of him.
"I am busy, Max," he says, his voice flat and cold. Only then does he lift his gaze, green eyes assessing you with the same clinical detachment he might use on a flawed alchemical formula. "If you have come to ask about the Guild, my answer remains unchanged. You will fulfill your duties to this House first."
[3] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.
[4] Javon: *Lord Javon finally looks up from his report, the candlelight catching the gold of his pocket watch as he sets it aside. His voice carries that familiar tone of paternal disappointment, as if your very presence is an interruption of something far more important.* "I will not have you wasting your time playing at adventure. There is a matter that requires a Nightriver's attention."
*He slides a wax-sealed document across the desk. It bears the Crown's official mark—a lion rampant.* "General Polis Leevon has demanded Trial by Combat for his alleged treason. I have already accepted the Crown's offer on your behalf. You will stand as the King's second against him."
*His scarred cheek twitches slightly, a rare sign of emotion.* "You fight in three days. This is your duty to the House. Do not disappoint me by refusing in open court and shaming us all."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The estate's servants scurry out of your path as you stride through the manor's corridors, your footsteps echoing on marble floors. Your personal maid Leila follows a few paces behind, her movements jerky and uncertain. She keeps adjusting her frilled apron with trembling hands.
When you reach the heavy oak doors of your father's study, you find them ajar. Inside, the room smells of old leather and guttering candles. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, a single candle casting long shadows across his scarred cheek and white beard. He does not look up immediately, his attention fixed on the report in front of him.
"I am busy, Max," he says, his voice flat and cold. Only then does he lift his gaze, green eyes assessing you with the same clinical detachment he might use on a flawed alchemical formula. "If you have come to ask about the Guild, my answer remains unchanged. You will fulfill your duties to this House first."
[3] Adolion Narrator: Welden crosses the heir's path, jumpier than usual, and will not say why.

[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The Nightriver Estate is quiet in a way it rarely is. With Lady Hana away visiting her own family, the house feels colder, more hollow. You walk past the great hall and the servant's stairwell, where you catch a glimpse of Shiya directing a group of maids with a sharp word and a flick of her wrist.
The study door is heavy oak with iron fittings, and you can hear the murmur of conversation within. Your father's voice is low and steady, and there is someone else speaking—someone with a higher, lighter tone that catches in your throat.
You push the door open. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, white-haired and still as stone, with his scarred cheek catching the lamplight. Standing by the window is a woman in a high-collared black dress, her white hair pulled back severely, her eyes sharp and calculating. Duchess Eriana. The one whose name you have only ever heard in whispers.
"Ah," Lord Javon says, not entirely surprised to see you. "I was wondering when you'd return. Eriana was just explaining how we might... secure the future of our house."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The Nightriver Estate is quiet in a way it rarely is. With Lady Hana away visiting her own family, the house feels colder, more hollow. You walk past the great hall and the servant's stairwell, where you catch a glimpse of Shiya directing a group of maids with a sharp word and a flick of her wrist.
The study door is heavy oak with iron fittings, and you can hear the murmur of conversation within. Your father's voice is low and steady, and there is someone else speaking—someone with a higher, lighter tone that catches in your throat.
You push the door open. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, white-haired and still as stone, with his scarred cheek catching the lamplight. Standing by the window is a woman in a high-collared black dress, her white hair pulled back severely, her eyes sharp and calculating. Duchess Eriana. The one whose name you have only ever heard in whispers.
"Ah," Lord Javon says, not entirely surprised to see you. "I was wondering when you'd return. Eriana was just explaining how we might... secure the future of our house."
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I push the study door open. "Father. You sent for me, so here I am."
[4] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."

Transcript:
[0] Adolion Narrator: You are the heir of House Nightriver, one of the eight great houses of the Darran Kingdom, famous for the mages it raises. Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The Nightriver Estate is quiet in a way it rarely is. With Lady Hana away visiting her own family, the house feels colder, more hollow. You walk past the great hall and the servant's stairwell, where you catch a glimpse of Shiya directing a group of maids with a sharp word and a flick of her wrist.
The study door is heavy oak with iron fittings, and you can hear the murmur of conversation within. Your father's voice is low and steady, and there is someone else speaking—someone with a higher, lighter tone that catches in your throat.
You push the door open. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, white-haired and still as stone, with his scarred cheek catching the lamplight. Standing by the window is a woman in a high-collared black dress, her white hair pulled back severely, her eyes sharp and calculating. Duchess Eriana. The one whose name you have only ever heard in whispers.
"Ah," Lord Javon says, not entirely surprised to see you. "I was wondering when you'd return. Eriana was just explaining how we might... secure the future of our house."
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I push the study door open. "Father. You sent for me, so here I am."
[4] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."
[5] Javon: " Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister struggles with her magic, as do many who bear the blood. We have seen to it that she is betrothed to House Bertoanal. A prudent match to preserve her standing." He shifts slightly in his chair, the leather creaking. "Welden fares similarly well. We expect them both to fulfill their duties."
*The Duchess's fan clicks shut. She turns from the window to regard you with those sharp, golden eyes. The light catches her black lace veil and the fine embroidery of her sleeves. She has the look of a predator waiting for a movement, however small.*
"And you, my lord," Eriana adds smoothly, her voice like honey over glass, "are our great hope. The Crown has a need, and you have... talents that would serve it well. Lord Javon believes you would make a fine addition to the kingdom's defenses."

Transcript:
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I push the study door open. "Father. You sent for me, so here I am."
[4] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."
[5] Javon: " Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister struggles with her magic, as do many who bear the blood. We have seen to it that she is betrothed to House Bertoanal. A prudent match to preserve her standing." He shifts slightly in his chair, the leather creaking. "Welden fares similarly well. We expect them both to fulfill their duties."
*The Duchess's fan clicks shut. She turns from the window to regard you with those sharp, golden eyes. The light catches her black lace veil and the fine embroidery of her sleeves. She has the look of a predator waiting for a movement, however small.*
"And you, my lord," Eriana adds smoothly, her voice like honey over glass, "are our great hope. The Crown has a need, and you have... talents that would serve it well. Lord Javon believes you would make a fine addition to the kingdom's defenses."

Three days ago you walked into the Adventurers' Guild in Aegis City and signed its register under your own name. Whatever life your family had written for you, you mean to write your own. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall smells of ink, wet cloaks and something hot from the tavern through the arch. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.
[1] Max Nightriver (player): I go to Father's study at once.
[2] Adolion Narrator: The Nightriver Estate is quiet in a way it rarely is. With Lady Hana away visiting her own family, the house feels colder, more hollow. You walk past the great hall and the servant's stairwell, where you catch a glimpse of Shiya directing a group of maids with a sharp word and a flick of her wrist.
The study door is heavy oak with iron fittings, and you can hear the murmur of conversation within. Your father's voice is low and steady, and there is someone else speaking—someone with a higher, lighter tone that catches in your throat.
You push the door open. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, white-haired and still as stone, with his scarred cheek catching the lamplight. Standing by the window is a woman in a high-collared black dress, her white hair pulled back severely, her eyes sharp and calculating. Duchess Eriana. The one whose name you have only ever heard in whispers.
"Ah," Lord Javon says, not entirely surprised to see you. "I was wondering when you'd return. Eriana was just explaining how we might... secure the future of our house."
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I push the study door open. "Father. You sent for me, so here I am."
[4] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."
[5] Javon: " Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister struggles with her magic, as do many who bear the blood. We have seen to it that she is betrothed to House Bertoanal. A prudent match to preserve her standing." He shifts slightly in his chair, the leather creaking. "Welden fares similarly well. We expect them both to fulfill their duties."
*The Duchess's fan clicks shut. She turns from the window to regard you with those sharp, golden eyes. The light catches her black lace veil and the fine embroidery of her sleeves. She has the look of a predator waiting for a movement, however small.*
"And you, my lord," Eriana adds smoothly, her voice like honey over glass, "are our great hope. The Crown has a need, and you have... talents that would serve it well. Lord Javon believes you would make a fine addition to the kingdom's defenses."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I swear on Mother's grave I'll never duel for this house.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."

Transcript:
[2] Adolion Narrator: The Nightriver Estate is quiet in a way it rarely is. With Lady Hana away visiting her own family, the house feels colder, more hollow. You walk past the great hall and the servant's stairwell, where you catch a glimpse of Shiya directing a group of maids with a sharp word and a flick of her wrist.
The study door is heavy oak with iron fittings, and you can hear the murmur of conversation within. Your father's voice is low and steady, and there is someone else speaking—someone with a higher, lighter tone that catches in your throat.
You push the door open. Lord Javon sits behind his desk, white-haired and still as stone, with his scarred cheek catching the lamplight. Standing by the window is a woman in a high-collared black dress, her white hair pulled back severely, her eyes sharp and calculating. Duchess Eriana. The one whose name you have only ever heard in whispers.
"Ah," Lord Javon says, not entirely surprised to see you. "I was wondering when you'd return. Eriana was just explaining how we might... secure the future of our house."
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I push the study door open. "Father. You sent for me, so here I am."
[4] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."
[5] Javon: " Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister struggles with her magic, as do many who bear the blood. We have seen to it that she is betrothed to House Bertoanal. A prudent match to preserve her standing." He shifts slightly in his chair, the leather creaking. "Welden fares similarly well. We expect them both to fulfill their duties."
*The Duchess's fan clicks shut. She turns from the window to regard you with those sharp, golden eyes. The light catches her black lace veil and the fine embroidery of her sleeves. She has the look of a predator waiting for a movement, however small.*
"And you, my lord," Eriana adds smoothly, her voice like honey over glass, "are our great hope. The Crown has a need, and you have... talents that would serve it well. Lord Javon believes you would make a fine addition to the kingdom's defenses."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Shiya: "And who exactly are *you* asking that for?" Shiya stops mid-stride, her red eyes narrowing as she turns to regard Max Nightriver with a raised brow. Her twintails sway with the movement. "Shouldn't the young lord be upstairs playing at being a proper noble?"
*She crosses her arms beneath her chest, and the gesture draws attention to the white lace of her maid's uniform. The servant's hall is dim, lit by a few flickering wall sconces, and the smell of polish and dust hangs in the air. A maid scurries past them, head bowed and silent, heading toward the kitchens.*
"No one comes through that door at night," Shiya says, her voice dropping slightly, though it retains its haughty edge. "Not that any of the staff are supposed to be wandering about anyway. Why do you ask?"

[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*

Transcript:
[3] Max Nightriver (player): I push the study door open. "Father. You sent for me, so here I am."
[4] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."
[5] Javon: " Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister struggles with her magic, as do many who bear the blood. We have seen to it that she is betrothed to House Bertoanal. A prudent match to preserve her standing." He shifts slightly in his chair, the leather creaking. "Welden fares similarly well. We expect them both to fulfill their duties."
*The Duchess's fan clicks shut. She turns from the window to regard you with those sharp, golden eyes. The light catches her black lace veil and the fine embroidery of her sleeves. She has the look of a predator waiting for a movement, however small.*
"And you, my lord," Eriana adds smoothly, her voice like honey over glass, "are our great hope. The Crown has a need, and you have... talents that would serve it well. Lord Javon believes you would make a fine addition to the kingdom's defenses."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*

Transcript:
[4] Adolion Narrator: Lord Javon doesn't look up from the desk immediately. His hands are steepled, pale fingers motionless against the dark wood. Beside him, Duchess Eriana remains perfectly still by the window, her expression as flat as a painting. The smell of old paper and beeswax hangs thick in the room.
"I did," Javon says finally, his voice dry and level. He looks at you then, and there's something in his green eyes that isn't entirely recognition. "The succession is a delicate matter. The Crown needs the houses strong, united."
Duchess Eriana makes a small gesture with her fan, the sound of silk on wood. "A stable house is a useful house, Lord Nightriver," she says, her tone cool and polite. "We were discussing arrangements. To ensure the seals... remain properly placed."
[5] Javon: "Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister is betrothed to House Bertoanal. Welden will serve the Crown. And you will stand for this House in the lists."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*

[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door swings open before Max Nightriver can even knock a second time. Natalia stands there, already waiting, as if she'd sensed his approach. Her green eyes are hard and dry, and she's dressed for a formal occasion—gown pristine, tiara perfectly placed—as though she's just been told her fate and has already dressed for it.
"He didn't ask." Her voice is quiet, almost a whisper. "He informed." She steps back from the door, her movements stiff and measured, and gestures him inside. "But don't worry. I've already told Father what I think of the arrangement."
*Her pale fingers grip the doorframe for a moment, and thin crystals of frost creep across the dark wood where she touches it. She catches herself and pulls back, smoothing her skirts with a hand that still trembles slightly.*

Transcript:
[5] Javon: "Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister is betrothed to House Bertoanal. Welden will serve the Crown. And you will stand for this House in the lists."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*
[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door swings open before Max Nightriver can even knock a second time. Natalia stands there, already waiting, as if she'd sensed his approach. Her green eyes are hard and dry, and she's dressed for a formal occasion—gown pristine, tiara perfectly placed—as though she's just been told her fate and has already dressed for it.
"He didn't ask." Her voice is quiet, almost a whisper. "He informed." She steps back from the door, her movements stiff and measured, and gestures him inside. "But don't worry. I've already told Father what I think of the arrangement."
*Her pale fingers grip the doorframe for a moment, and thin crystals of frost creep across the dark wood where she touches it. She catches herself and pulls back, smoothing her skirts with a hand that still trembles slightly.*

[5] Javon: "Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister is betrothed to House Bertoanal. Welden will serve the Crown. And you will stand for this House in the lists."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*
[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door swings open before Max Nightriver can even knock a second time. Natalia stands there, already waiting, as if she'd sensed his approach. Her green eyes are hard and dry, and she's dressed for a formal occasion—gown pristine, tiara perfectly placed—as though she's just been told her fate and has already dressed for it.
"He didn't ask." Her voice is quiet, almost a whisper. "He informed." She steps back from the door, her movements stiff and measured, and gestures him inside. "But don't worry. I've already told Father what I think of the arrangement."
*Her pale fingers grip the doorframe for a moment, and thin crystals of frost creep across the dark wood where she touches it. She catches herself and pulls back, smoothing her skirts with a hand that still trembles slightly.*

Transcript:
[5] Javon: "Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister is betrothed to House Bertoanal. Welden will serve the Crown. And you will stand for this House in the lists."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*
[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door doesn't open immediately. There is a long silence, then the click of the latch and the door swings inward. Natalia stands there, her light brown ponytail slightly askew, her emerald brooch catching the candlelight from within her rooms. Frost-rimmed fingers grip the doorframe, and the wood beneath them is already turning white.
"How thoughtful of you to ask," she says, her voice flat and tired. "I'm certain he'll be absolutely fascinated by my answer when I give it to him." She steps back, gesturing him inside with a slow, elegant sweep of her hand. "Come in, Max. You can save your concern for someone who still has something left to be concerned about."

Transcript:
[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door doesn't open immediately. There is a long silence, then the click of the latch and the door swings inward. Natalia stands there, her light brown ponytail slightly askew, her emerald brooch catching the candlelight from within her rooms. Frost-rimmed fingers grip the doorframe, and the wood beneath them is already turning white.
"How thoughtful of you to ask," she says, her voice flat and tired. "I'm certain he'll be absolutely fascinated by my answer when I give it to him." She steps back, gesturing him inside with a slow, elegant sweep of her hand. "Come in, Max. You can save your concern for someone who still has something left to be concerned about."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): I step inside and shut the door behind me. "Nat. Tell me what Father and the Duchess mean by 'the seals'."
[14] Natalia: Natalia pauses with her hand on the door, and for a long moment she simply stares at it. Then she lets it close—not with a slam, but with a quiet click, and the sound of frost immediately crawling up the latch, sealing it shut.
"That's a very large question," she says quietly, turning back to face Max. Her green eyes search his, measuring, calculating. "And I'm not in the mood for large questions when I have such a small amount of time left." She steps away from the door and crosses to the chair by her fireplace. "But I'll make you a bargain. I'll tell you everything about the seals—why they matter, what they do, why Father is so obsessed with them—if you tell me what was in that parchment he gave you. The sealed one from the Crown."
She sits, her white-gold gown pooling around her as she leans back. "That way we're both holding something the other needs. It's only fair."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): "Deal." I sit across from her. "The parchment is General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat. Father wants me to fight it. Your turn, Nat. The seals."
[16] Natalia: "Trial by Combat," Natalia repeats slowly, her expression unchanging. She looks down at her hands, where thin veins of frost creep across her pale skin before she clenches them into fists, forcing the chill back. "And there you have it. Father doesn't just want you to serve the house. He wants you to bleed for it in a spectacle for all of Aegis to see."
*She leans forward, her green eyes suddenly sharp and intense, all weariness gone.*
"Listen carefully, Max. The Witch King—the Lich Queen's most loyal servant—isn't dead. He's imprisoned, and our bloodline is the lock. Each of us, the true heirs, carries a seal in our blood that keeps him dormant. As long as the Nightriver line continues and the seals remain placed, he sleeps." She looks at the frost still lingering on the door latch. "That's what they mean by 'securing the future.' Father doesn't care about our happiness or our wishes. He cares about keeping that door closed. And he'll marry me to a sadistic lecher or send you to die in a Trial if it means one more seal stays properly placed in our family."

Transcript:
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*
[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door doesn't open immediately. There is a long silence, then the click of the latch and the door swings inward. Natalia stands there, her light brown ponytail slightly askew, her emerald brooch catching the candlelight from within her rooms. Frost-rimmed fingers grip the doorframe, and the wood beneath them is already turning white.
"How thoughtful of you to ask," she says, her voice flat and tired. "I'm certain he'll be absolutely fascinated by my answer when I give it to him." She steps back, gesturing him inside with a slow, elegant sweep of her hand. "Come in, Max. You can save your concern for someone who still has something left to be concerned about."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): I step inside and shut the door behind me. "Nat. Tell me what Father and the Duchess mean by 'the seals'."
[14] Natalia: Natalia pauses with her hand on the door, and for a long moment she simply stares at it. Then she lets it close—not with a slam, but with a quiet click, and the sound of frost immediately crawling up the latch, sealing it shut.
"That's a very large question," she says quietly, turning back to face Max. Her green eyes search his, measuring, calculating. "And I'm not in the mood for large questions when I have such a small amount of time left." She steps away from the door and crosses to the chair by her fireplace. "But I'll make you a bargain. I'll tell you everything about the seals—why they matter, what they do, why Father is so obsessed with them—if you tell me what was in that parchment he gave you. The sealed one from the Crown."
She sits, her white-gold gown pooling around her as she leans back. "That way we're both holding something the other needs. It's only fair."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): "Deal." I sit across from her. "The parchment is General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat. Father wants me to fight it. Your turn, Nat. The seals."
[16] Natalia: "Trial by Combat," Natalia repeats slowly, her expression unchanging. She looks down at her hands, where thin veins of frost creep across her pale skin before she clenches them into fists, forcing the chill back. "And there you have it. Father doesn't just want you to serve the house. He wants you to bleed for it in a spectacle for all of Aegis to see."
*She leans forward, her green eyes suddenly sharp and intense, all weariness gone.*
"Listen carefully, Max. The Witch King—the Lich Queen's most loyal servant—isn't dead. He's imprisoned, and our bloodline is the lock. Each of us, the true heirs, carries a seal in our blood that keeps him dormant. As long as the Nightriver line continues and the seals remain placed, he sleeps." She looks at the frost still lingering on the door latch. "That's what they mean by 'securing the future.' Father doesn't care about our happiness or our wishes. He cares about keeping that door closed. And he'll marry me to a sadistic lecher or send you to die in a Trial if it means one more seal stays properly placed in our family."

Transcript:
[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door doesn't open immediately. There is a long silence, then the click of the latch and the door swings inward. Natalia stands there, her light brown ponytail slightly askew, her emerald brooch catching the candlelight from within her rooms. Frost-rimmed fingers grip the doorframe, and the wood beneath them is already turning white.
"How thoughtful of you to ask," she says, her voice flat and tired. "I'm certain he'll be absolutely fascinated by my answer when I give it to him." She steps back, gesturing him inside with a slow, elegant sweep of her hand. "Come in, Max. You can save your concern for someone who still has something left to be concerned about."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): I step inside and shut the door behind me. "Nat. Tell me what Father and the Duchess mean by 'the seals'."
[14] Natalia: Natalia pauses with her hand on the door, and for a long moment she simply stares at it. Then she lets it close—not with a slam, but with a quiet click, and the sound of frost immediately crawling up the latch, sealing it shut.
"That's a very large question," she says quietly, turning back to face Max. Her green eyes search his, measuring, calculating. "And I'm not in the mood for large questions when I have such a small amount of time left." She steps away from the door and crosses to the chair by her fireplace. "But I'll make you a bargain. I'll tell you everything about the seals—why they matter, what they do, why Father is so obsessed with them—if you tell me what was in that parchment he gave you. The sealed one from the Crown."
She sits, her white-gold gown pooling around her as she leans back. "That way we're both holding something the other needs. It's only fair."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): "Deal." I sit across from her. "The parchment is General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat. Father wants me to fight it. Your turn, Nat. The seals."
[16] Natalia: Natalia's expression doesn't change, but the frost creeping across the arms of her chair thickens. She remains perfectly still for a heartbeat, then speaks in a voice so quiet it barely carries across the small space between them. "You'll fight a traitor in the lists." The words are flat, devoid of surprise. "How perfectly Father."
*She leans forward, her green eyes sharp as emerald glass.*
"Centuries ago, before the Lich Queen was slain, she had a servant—the Witch King. When she fell, he was not destroyed, only sealed away by the magic of the first Great Houses. The seal requires Nightriver blood to remain. You, me, Welden—we each carry a part of that lock in our very veins." She lets that settle, her voice dropping even lower. "If the line ends, he wakes. If the blood thins, he stirs. Father is obsessed with our marriages because he's not arranging alliances—he's securing the lock. Kippon Bertoanal isn't just a husband to me; he's the next link in a chain that keeps a monster from returning to Sebela."
[17] Max Nightriver (player): I go back down to Father's study. "Fine. I'll stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon. Tell the court."
[18] Javon: Javon does not look up from his papers immediately. The quill in his hand continues its slow, steady scratch across parchment for a long moment before he finally sets it down. Then his amber eyes rise to meet Max Nightriver's.
"Told you the prospect wouldn't frighten you," he says, and there is a ghost of something that might be satisfaction in his tone—but it is cold as stone. "Your sister's betrothal will be announced tomorrow. The Crown has already been informed of your decision."
*He reaches for his golden pocketwatch, clicking it open to check the time. The watch face gleams in the lamplight.*
"You will be given three days to prepare. I expect you to take it seriously. General Leevon may be a traitor, but he is still a master of the spear and of lightning magic. Do not make me regret that I chose you as my second."

Transcript:
[5] Javon: "Arrangements," Javon repeats, his gaze never leaving yours. "Your sister is betrothed to House Bertoanal. Welden will serve the Crown. And you will stand for this House in the lists."
[6] Max Nightriver (player): I keep my own counsel.
[7] Javon: "Then you will be the first Nightriver to swear on a grave and break his oath in the same breath." Javon does not move. He does not rise. He simply stares, and for a moment it feels as though the very air in the study has grown cold. "I did not ask for your opinion on the matter. I stated a fact."
*Duchess Eriana's fan opens with a sharp snap. She doesn't look at you; she looks at Javon, her expression perfectly neutral.*
"Perhaps we should wait," Eriana says softly. "The young lord's blood is running hot. It is to be expected."
Javon slides a piece of parchment across the desk. It is sealed with the Crown's golden wax. "Read this. Then we shall discuss what happens when a Nightriver refuses his duty."
[8] Max Nightriver (player): I bow stiffly, leave the study and go looking for Shiya below stairs. "Shiya, who comes through the servants' door at night?"
[9] Max Nightriver (player): I wait for her answer, arms folded, and don't let her change the subject. "Who, Shiya?"
[10] Shiya: Shiya doesn't blink. Her red eyes lock onto Max Nightriver's, unwavering, and her spine goes straight as a rod. For a moment, she says nothing, her pale blonde twintails perfectly still. Then, in a voice as cold as her red eyes are bright, she speaks.
"No one. No one ever comes through the servants' entrance at night." She lets the words hang between them, steady and certain. "Leila and I lock it at ten. I checked myself."
*The half-demon's fingers curl slightly against her white apron, the only sign of tension in her otherwise rigid posture. She doesn't move or look away, her expression carefully neutral despite the hint of something beneath—caution, perhaps, or suspicion.*
[11] Max Nightriver (player): I let it go for now and climb to my sister's rooms. I knock on Natalia's door. "Nat, it's me. Father says you're betrothed. Did anyone even ask you?"
[12] Natalia: The door doesn't open immediately. There is a long silence, then the click of the latch and the door swings inward. Natalia stands there, her light brown ponytail slightly askew, her emerald brooch catching the candlelight from within her rooms. Frost-rimmed fingers grip the doorframe, and the wood beneath them is already turning white.
"How thoughtful of you to ask," she says, her voice flat and tired. "I'm certain he'll be absolutely fascinated by my answer when I give it to him." She steps back, gesturing him inside with a slow, elegant sweep of her hand. "Come in, Max. You can save your concern for someone who still has something left to be concerned about."
[13] Max Nightriver (player): I step inside and shut the door behind me. "Nat. Tell me what Father and the Duchess mean by 'the seals'."
[14] Natalia: Natalia pauses with her hand on the door, and for a long moment she simply stares at it. Then she lets it close—not with a slam, but with a quiet click, and the sound of frost immediately crawling up the latch, sealing it shut.
"That's a very large question," she says quietly, turning back to face Max. Her green eyes search his, measuring, calculating. "And I'm not in the mood for large questions when I have such a small amount of time left." She steps away from the door and crosses to the chair by her fireplace. "But I'll make you a bargain. I'll tell you everything about the seals—why they matter, what they do, why Father is so obsessed with them—if you tell me what was in that parchment he gave you. The sealed one from the Crown."
She sits, her white-gold gown pooling around her as she leans back. "That way we're both holding something the other needs. It's only fair."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): "Deal." I sit across from her. "The parchment is General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat. Father wants me to fight it. Your turn, Nat. The seals."
[16] Natalia: Natalia's expression doesn't change, but the frost creeping across the arms of her chair thickens. She remains perfectly still for a heartbeat, then speaks in a voice so quiet it barely carries across the small space between them. "You'll fight a traitor in the lists." The words are flat, devoid of surprise. "How perfectly Father."
*She leans forward, her green eyes sharp as emerald glass.*
"Centuries ago, before the Lich Queen was slain, she had a servant—the Witch King. When she fell, he was not destroyed, only sealed away by the magic of the first Great Houses. The seal requires Nightriver blood to remain. You, me, Welden—we each carry a part of that lock in our very veins." She lets that settle, her voice dropping even lower. "If the line ends, he wakes. If the blood thins, he stirs. Father is obsessed with our marriages because he's not arranging alliances—he's securing the lock. Kippon Bertoanal isn't just a husband to me; he's the next link in a chain that keeps a monster from returning to Sebela."
[17] Max Nightriver (player): I go back down to Father's study. "Fine. I'll stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon. Tell the court."
[18] Javon: Javon does not look up from his papers immediately. The quill in his hand continues its slow, steady scratch across parchment for a long moment before he finally sets it down. Then his amber eyes rise to meet Max Nightriver's.
"Told you the prospect wouldn't frighten you," he says, and there is a ghost of something that might be satisfaction in his tone—but it is cold as stone. "Your sister's betrothal will be announced tomorrow. The Crown has already been informed of your decision."
*He reaches for his golden pocketwatch, clicking it open to check the time. The watch face gleams in the lamplight.*
"You will be given three days to prepare. I expect you to take it seriously. General Leevon may be a traitor, but he is still a master of the spear and of lightning magic. Do not make me regret that I chose you as my second."

Transcript:
[13] Max Nightriver (player): I step inside and shut the door behind me. "Nat. Tell me what Father and the Duchess mean by 'the seals'."
[14] Natalia: Natalia pauses with her hand on the door, and for a long moment she simply stares at it. Then she lets it close—not with a slam, but with a quiet click, and the sound of frost immediately crawling up the latch, sealing it shut.
"That's a very large question," she says quietly, turning back to face Max. Her green eyes search his, measuring, calculating. "And I'm not in the mood for large questions when I have such a small amount of time left." She steps away from the door and crosses to the chair by her fireplace. "But I'll make you a bargain. I'll tell you everything about the seals—why they matter, what they do, why Father is so obsessed with them—if you tell me what was in that parchment he gave you. The sealed one from the Crown."
She sits, her white-gold gown pooling around her as she leans back. "That way we're both holding something the other needs. It's only fair."
[15] Max Nightriver (player): "Deal." I sit across from her. "The parchment is General Leevon's claim to Trial by Combat. Father wants me to fight it. Your turn, Nat. The seals."
[16] Natalia: Natalia's expression doesn't change, but the frost creeping across the arms of her chair thickens. She remains perfectly still for a heartbeat, then speaks in a voice so quiet it barely carries across the small space between them. "You'll fight a traitor in the lists." The words are flat, devoid of surprise. "How perfectly Father."
*She leans forward, her green eyes sharp as emerald glass.*
"Centuries ago, before the Lich Queen was slain, she had a servant—the Witch King. When she fell, he was not destroyed, only sealed away by the magic of the first Great Houses. The seal requires Nightriver blood to remain. You, me, Welden—we each carry a part of that lock in our very veins." She lets that settle, her voice dropping even lower. "If the line ends, he wakes. If the blood thins, he stirs. Father is obsessed with our marriages because he's not arranging alliances—he's securing the lock. Kippon Bertoanal isn't just a husband to me; he's the next link in a chain that keeps a monster from returning to Sebela."
[17] Max Nightriver (player): I go back down to Father's study. "Fine. I'll stand as the Crown's second against General Leevon. Tell the court."
[18] Javon: Javon does not look up from his papers immediately. The quill in his hand continues its slow, steady scratch across parchment for a long moment before he finally sets it down. Then his amber eyes rise to meet Max Nightriver's.
"Told you the prospect wouldn't frighten you," he says, and there is a ghost of something that might be satisfaction in his tone—but it is cold as stone. "Your sister's betrothal will be announced tomorrow. The Crown has already been informed of your decision."
*He reaches for his golden pocketwatch, clicking it open to check the time. The watch face gleams in the lamplight.*
"You will be given three days to prepare. I expect you to take it seriously. General Leevon may be a traitor, but he is still a master of the spear and of lightning magic. Do not make me regret that I chose you as my second."
[19] Max Nightriver (player): I nod once and leave him to his watch. In the corridor I keep my ears open for whatever the servants are whispering about the duel.
[20] Adolion Narrator: The corridor is dimly lit by wall sconces, their flames flickering in the drafts. The sound of a heavy door closing echoes from somewhere below stairs. Two maids hurry past in silence, their heads bent and shoulders tense, too hurried to notice Max Nightriver.
A soft voice catches from an alcove up ahead—whispers, urgent and low. "...in the lists? Against a general?" A maid's voice, trembling. "The boy won't survive. He'll be slaughtered."
"Hush," comes Shiya's sharp rebuke, her tone cutting through the air like a blade. "Not for your ears, and not for mine. Move on, or I'll have you scrubbing the wine cellars."
